title: Three Exceptions, Then Queen Helene's Sukkah
subtitle: Why each sage rejected the other two sources, three width/size exceptions, and R' Yehuda's proof from a real sukkah.
sources: Gemara text: Sefaria (William Davidson Edition). Structure cross-checked against the Dafyomi Advancement Forum (dafyomi.co.il) and Talmud Navigator for Sukkah 2. The final point below continues onto 3a.
before: 2a gave three reasons — Rabbah, Rebbi Zeira, Rava — for the same 20-amos line. This amud opens by asking why each of them didn't just accept one of the other two verses.

Then three more sages each cite a case where a sukkah stays kosher above 20 amos anyway, and the Gemara has to work out which of 2a's three reasons each exception actually fits — before turning to R' Yehuda's own proof that the line can be pushed to 40–50 amos.

flow.label: Gemara asks why each sage rejected the other two verses
flow.sub: Rabbah's verse: read as "future generations," not live awareness · Zeira's verse: read as about the messianic era · Rava's verse: weakened by Abaye's iron-wall question

flowCaption: Each reason from 2a gets tested against a real exception, before the Gemara turns to R' Yehuda's own proof.

opinions.claim: The dispute over 20 amos applies only where the walls don't reach the sechach. If the walls do reach the sechach, the sukkah is fit even above 20 amos.
opinions.basis: Fits Rabbah: the eye follows the walls up to the roofing, so it's still "noticed."

opinions.claim: The dispute applies only to a sukkah no larger than 4×4 amos. Larger than that, it's fit even above 20 amos.
opinions.basis: Fits Rebbi Zeira: a spacious sukkah still gets real shade from its own roofing.

opinions.claim: The dispute applies only to a sukkah barely large enough to hold a person's head, most of his body, and his table. Larger than that, it's fit even above 20 amos.
opinions.basis: Matches none of Rabbah, Rebbi Zeira, or Rava's stated reasons.

script.speaker: Gemara explains
script.quote: כּוּלְּהוּ כְּרַבָּה לָא אָמְרִי, הָהוּא יְדִיעָה לְדוֹרוֹת הִיא.
script.gloss: Rebbi Zeira and Rava didn't adopt Rabbah's verse, because in their view it isn't about a live requirement to perceive the sukkah — it's about future generations knowing (historically) about the Exodus.

script.speaker: Gemara explains
script.quote: כְּרַבִּי זֵירָא נָמֵי לָא אָמְרִי, הָהוּא לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ הוּא דִּכְתִיב.
script.gloss: Rabbah and Rava didn't adopt Rebbi Zeira's verse, because in their view that verse in Isaiah refers to the messianic era, not the physical construction of a sukkah.

script.speaker: Gemara asks
script.gloss: How would Rebbi Zeira answer that?

script.speaker: Rebbi Zeira (defense)
script.quote: אִם כֵּן לֵימָא קְרָא: וְחוּפָּה תִּהְיֶה לְצֵל יוֹמָם, וּמַאי וְסוּכָּה תִּהְיֶה לְצֵל יוֹמָם — שָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ תַּרְתֵּי.
script.gloss: If it only meant the messianic era, the verse should have said "canopy," not "sukkah." Since it specifically says "sukkah," learn two things from it at once — the messianic promise, and that a sukkah's own roofing must give shade.

script.speaker: Gemara explains
script.quote: כְּרָבָא נָמֵי לָא אָמְרִי, מִשּׁוּם קוּשְׁיָא דְאַבָּיֵי.
script.gloss: Rabbah and Rebbi Zeira didn't adopt Rava's verse either, because of the difficulty Abaye raised about iron walls.

script.speaker: Gemara asks
script.quote: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה אָמַר רַב: מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּשֶׁאֵין דְּפָנוֹת מַגִּיעוֹת לַסְּכָךְ, אֲבָל דְּפָנוֹת מַגִּיעוֹת לַסְּכָךְ — אֲפִילּוּ לְמַעְלָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה כְּשֵׁרָה.
script.gloss: Whose opinion does Rabbi Yoshiya's ruling follow — that the dispute is only where the walls don't reach the sechach, but if they do, the sukkah is fit even above 20 amos?

script.speaker: Answer
script.quote: כְּרַבָּה, דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא שָׁלְטָא בַּהּ עֵינָא, וְכֵיוָן דִּדְפָנוֹת מַגִּיעוֹת לַסְּכָךְ, מִשְׁלָט שָׁלְטָא בַּהּ עֵינָא.
script.gloss: Rabbah's — since his reasoning is that the eye doesn't naturally catch the sechach; once the walls reach the sechach, the eye follows them up and does catch it.

script.speaker: Gemara asks
script.quote: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּשֶׁאֵין בָּהּ אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת עַל אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, אֲבָל יֵשׁ בָּהּ יוֹתֵר ... אֲפִילּוּ לְמַעְלָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה כְּשֵׁרָה.
script.gloss: Whose opinion does Rav Huna's ruling follow — that the dispute is only for a sukkah no bigger than 4×4 amos, but larger than that it's fit even above 20 amos?

script.speaker: Answer
script.quote: כְּרַבִּי זֵירָא, דְּאָמַר: מִשּׁוּם צֵל הוּא, וְכֵיוָן דִּרְוִיחָא — אִיכָּא צֵל סוּכָּה.
script.gloss: Rebbi Zeira's — since his reasoning is about shade; a spacious sukkah still gets real shade from its own roofing, not just its walls.

script.speaker: Gemara asks
script.quote: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רַבָּה אָמַר רַב: מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּשֶׁאֵינָהּ מַחְזֶקֶת אֶלָּא כְּדֵי רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ וְשׁוּלְחָנוֹ ... כְּמַאן?
script.gloss: Whose opinion does Rav Chanan bar Rabah's ruling follow — that the dispute is only for a sukkah barely holding a person's head, most of his body, and his table?

script.speaker: Answer
script.gloss: Not in accordance with any one of them (Rabbah, Rebbi Zeira, or Rava) — this ruling doesn't match any of the three stated reasons.

script.speaker: Gemara asks
script.gloss: Fine — Rabbi Yoshiya clearly differs from Rav Huna and Rav Chanan bar Rabah, since they measure by floor area and he doesn't. But do Rav Huna and Rav Chanan bar Rabah disagree about the minimum size for a kosher sukkah itself — one holding it's 4×4 amos, the other holding it's "head, most of the body, and table"?

script.speaker: Answer
script.gloss: No — everyone agrees the minimum kosher sukkah is "head, most of the body, and table." They disagree only about where the height-dispute range sits: Rav Chanan bar Rabah says the dispute is only right at that bare minimum, and anything larger is fit regardless of height. Rav Huna says the dispute runs from that bare minimum all the way up to 4×4 amos, and only past 4×4 amos is it fit regardless of height.

script.speaker: Beraita objects
script.quote: סוּכָּה שֶׁהִיא גְּבוֹהָה לְמַעְלָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה — פְּסוּלָה, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַכְשִׁיר עַד אַרְבָּעִים וַחֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה.
script.gloss: A sukkah over 20 amos is unfit — R' Yehuda deems it fit up to 40–50 amos.

script.speaker: R' Yehuda's proof
script.quote: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּהֵילֶנִי הַמַּלְכָּה בְּלוֹד שֶׁהָיְתָה סוּכָּתָהּ גְּבוֹהָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה, וְהָיוּ זְקֵנִים נִכְנָסִין וְיוֹצְאִין לְשָׁם וְלֹא אָמְרוּ לָהּ דָּבָר.
script.gloss: There was an incident involving Queen Helene in Lod, whose sukkah was more than 20 amos high — and the Elders went in and out of it and said nothing.

script.speaker: Challenge
script.quote: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָיה? אִשָּׁה הָיְתָה וּפְטוּרָה מִן הַסּוּכָּה.
script.gloss: Is that a proof? She was a woman, and women are exempt from the sukkah obligation.

script.speaker: Defense
script.quote: וַהֲלֹא שִׁבְעָה בָּנִים הֲווֹ לָהּ, וְעוֹד: כׇּל מַעֲשֶׂיהָ לֹא עָשְׂתָה אֶלָּא עַל פִּי חֲכָמִים.
script.gloss: Didn't she have seven sons — who required a fit sukkah? And furthermore, everything she did followed the guidance of the Sages.

script.speaker: Gemara asks
script.gloss: Why does R' Yehuda need that second point ("she followed the Sages") — wasn't the seven-sons point enough?

script.speaker: Answer
script.gloss: If you'd say her sons were all minors (exempt), since she had seven of them, at least one must have reached the age of "no longer needing his mother" — obligated by rabbinic law. And if you'd say that obligation is only rabbinic and she may not have followed rabbinic law — that's exactly what the second point answers: she followed the Sages in everything.
